column7: Typo – Absolute lexicographical parameters strictly dictate that the base noun for fine woven silk is *dukūlam* (with a long 'ū'). The structurally compromised string must be algebraically corrected to *sudukūlaiḥ* to mathematically re-establish absolute orthographic isomorphism.

column6: kusumbhaḥ Mere outward affection (compared with the colour of safflower);
column7: Typo – Please note that the above definition is restricted to "Masculine" gender only! Therefore the middle portion "-mbham", seems confusing. But maybe you like it that way!

Typo – Please note that this correction is suggested for the "Modern Spelling" !  A Dictionary should be useful for the Modern day! I am aware that Andhrabharati generally prefers the "Old-Fashioned" spellings. Ah, but there is the saying, "Be Here Now" ! In fact, there is only "Now" – Yesterday and Tomorrow are BOTH simply ideas in the "Now"!  Andhrabharati's penchant for "Old-Fashioned" spellings, is simply an "Old-Fashioned" idea being retained in the "Now" ! HE prefers to carry the "anuvṛtti" of "what was", rather than the free and effortless fact of "what is" !
